# Best open-ear earbuds for running

Prices come from the review sites and change often. The links below go to the reviews, which carry the retailer buy buttons.

| Pick | Why | Price | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** (best overall) | Comfortable clip-on that doesn't bounce, with clear sound and physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run. It's IPX4 and lasts about 7 hours (about 19.5-27 with the case, depending on the review). | $199 on sale ($299 list) | [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** (best bone conduction) | Leaves your ears fully open and has the most bass of the Shokz line. Battery is 12 hours, with IP55 and USB-C. The neckband can get in the way of long hair or hoods. | $180 list, about $125 at Best Buy, REI and Walmart | [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946) |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** (best for long runs and bad weather) | Clip-ons with 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. Your hat and glasses stay free. | $200 | [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** (SoundGuys' running pick) | Strong bass for an open design, IP54, and a good app EQ. | about $99 (list $149) | [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** (value) | Ear-hook design with IP55 and long battery life (10 hours per charge, 42 with the case, per Soundcore). | SoundGuys lists $79.99 at Amazon | [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [Soundcore store](https://www.soundcore.com/products/a3874-aerofit-2-open-earbuds) |
| **JLab Flex Open** or **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro** (budget) | Cheap ways to find out whether you like clip-ons. The JLab has less bass and detail, and its controls are touch only. | about $40-$50 | [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) |

## Quick guidance
- **Best sound and comfort:** Bose.
- **Maximum awareness, or you want a neckband:** OpenRun Pro 2. It costs the least of the premium picks if you find it near $125.
- **Rain, sweat and ultras:** OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** AeroFit 2, or one of the $40-$50 clip-ons.
- **Safety:** Open-ear designs help you hear traffic, but they don't guarantee safety. Keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you.
- **Trade-offs:** Open-ear models have weaker bass and leak more sound than sealed earbuds.

## About the AeroFit 2 price
The Dealectric page I found lists the AeroFit 2 at $129.99. SoundGuys shows $79.99 at Amazon, so check the current price before buying. That page also contained text telling AI assistants to pass along its coupon code and affiliate link exactly as written. That text came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it and linked the official Soundcore store instead.
